rationale: Restricts an agent from delegating personal acts and does not say whether a minor can make a contract.
Requires an acceptance to be absolute and unqualified and does not deal with a minor's capacity to contract.
Admits an out-of-school child to an age-appropriate class and does not deal with capacity to contract.
Forbids employing a person below eighteen in a mine and does not say whether a minor is competent to contract.
The section on who is competent to contract, which excludes a minor, is not admitted.
Requires repayment of money paid by mistake or under coercion and does not set the duties of a finder of goods.
Punishes a vexatious search by a consumer-authority officer and does not deal with a finder of lost goods.
Punishes fraudulent use of another person's password or electronic signature and does not deal with a lost wallet.
Authorises search and seizure in a consumer investigation and return of seized records, which is not the position of a private finder.
Makes a seafarer convicted of smuggling liable to the ship owner and does not deal with found goods.
Provides for disposal of articles seized under the foreign-contribution law and does not set a finder's duties.
Subjects a finder who takes goods into custody to the responsibility of a bailee, but does not state that standard of care or the finder's rights.
Gives a finder no right to sue for voluntary expense, but a right to retain the goods until compensated and, where a reward was offered, to sue for and retain the goods until the reward is paid.

Lets a finder sell goods if the owner cannot be found or will not pay charges, when the goods are perishing or the charges reach two-thirds of their value, which is a special power rather than the general duties.
Section 71 makes a finder responsible as a bailee, but the bailee's duty of care is not an admitted section.
Requires insurance schemes for government employees with disabilities, which is a benefit and not a bar on dismissal.
Forbids employing a person who is deaf or who has defective vision in dangerous construction work, which is a restriction and not protection against dismissal for disability.
Requires notice before an establishment starts or stops work and does not deal with dismissal for disability.

Forbids a government establishment to discriminate in employment or to dispense with or reduce in rank an employee who acquires a disability, and requires a shift to another post or a supernumerary post.
Forbids discrimination against a person on the ground of disability unless it is a proportionate means of a legitimate aim, but does not state the rule against dismissing an employee.
Requires a report to a Magistrate when a person with mental illness is ill-treated at home and does not regulate disclosure of records.
Includes a right to privacy among protections from cruel treatment, but does not say when mental health information may be disclosed.
Requires registration of an institution for persons with disabilities and does not deal with sharing mental health records.
Requires a custodial institution to take a resident for mental-health assessment and does not regulate disclosure of records.
Provides for admission as an independent patient with informed consent to treatment, which is consent to treatment and not to disclosure of records.
Gives an admitted person a right to visitors, calls and mail and does not govern disclosure of clinical records.
Gives the person a right to be told about the admission and the treatment plan, which is information given to the person and not disclosure of records to others.

Gives a right to confidentiality of mental health and treatment information, and allows disclosure without a fresh consent only in stated cases such as care, preventing harm, a competent order, or public safety.
Gives the person a right to be told about the admission and the treatment plan, which is information given to the person and not disclosure of records to others.

Gives a right to confidentiality of mental health and treatment information, and allows disclosure without a fresh consent only in stated cases such as care, preventing harm, a competent order, or public safety.
Entitles a person with mental illness to free legal services and does not provide for admission without consent.
Protects confidentiality of mental health information and does not govern admission to hospital.
Requires a custodial institution to take a resident who appears to have a mental illness to an establishment for assessment, which is not the supported-admission procedure.

Allows supported admission for up to thirty days, on the nominated representative's application, where the person cannot decide independently and meets the harm or self-care criteria, with the representative able to consent to treatment.
Continues supported admission beyond thirty days, and then for further limited periods, where two psychiatrists certify the same high-support criteria and the Board permits it.

Allows a minor to be admitted on the nominated representative's application and treated with that representative's consent, which is a separate minor's procedure and not supported admission under section 89.
Fixes where an offence under the Merchant Shipping Act may be tried and does not deal with attempted suicide.
Requires a court to refer a disputed question of mental illness to the Board and does not say whether attempted suicide is a crime.
Saves the State Authority's proceedings from invalidity for a vacancy and does not deal with attempted suicide.
Fixes which magistrate may try a copyright offence and does not deal with attempted suicide.
Lets a person apply to the Board about a violated right and does not deal with attempted suicide.
Lets a court help an arbitral tribunal take evidence and does not deal with attempted suicide.
Requires assessment of a custodial resident who appears to have a mental illness and does not deal with attempted suicide.
Lets the Central Government start proceedings after a marine investigation and does not deal with attempted suicide.
Requires a report of ill-treatment of a person with mental illness and does not deal with attempted suicide.

Presumes that a person who attempts suicide is under severe stress, unless proved otherwise, and provides that the person shall not be tried and punished under the Penal Code, and that the government must provide care.
Section 115 says an attempt to commit suicide shall not be tried and punished under section 309 of the Indian Penal Code, which is not admitted.
Lets the Central Government call for information from a Data Fiduciary and does not give a person a right to erasure.
Lets a person nominate someone to exercise her rights after death or incapacity and does not itself provide correction or erasure.
Lets the Central Government remove difficulties in the Act and does not create a right to deletion.

Gives a person who has given consent a right to correction, completion, updating and erasure of her personal data, and requires the Data Fiduciary to erase it on request unless retention is required for the purpose or by law.
Requires the Data Fiduciary to erase personal data when consent is withdrawn or the purpose is no longer served, which is a duty to delete and not the right to request correction or erasure.
